title: Ape Escape 3: turning a television studio into a capture playground
summary: Ape Escape 3 frames its gadget-led platforming as a show within a show. The player switches between specialized transformations, pursues monkeys through themed sets, and uses the DualShock 2’s twin sticks to control the capture net and camera. The result is a sequel whose comic television premise gives structure to a surprisingly varied toolkit.

blocks.text: A broadcast supplies the level logic

The fictional Monkey White television network gives the game a reason to move between sharply different environments. A stage can borrow the look of a genre or production set, so changing scenery feels like a programming choice rather than a disconnected collection of levels. The joke also gives the player a frame for the pursuit: the monkeys have taken over entertainment, and the hero’s work is to disrupt the broadcast by catching them.

Ape Escape’s signature control idea remains the foundation: one stick moves the character while the other operates the net. This division asks players to coordinate movement and tool direction instead of relying on a context-sensitive button. In Ape Escape 3, the principle supports a more demanding set of encounters, where a monkey may run, hide, or use the stage itself to evade capture. The control scheme keeps the chase physical and immediate.

The game’s special suits grant distinct abilities, letting the player answer obstacles with different actions. Rather than merely adding another weapon, a transformation can alter how a space is traversed or how an enemy is approached. That creates a compact form of progression: new verbs expand the ways a familiar stage layout can be read. The television themes help signal which abilities and comic situations a level is likely to emphasize.

Capturing monkeys is both the mission goal and the source of the game’s comic rhythm. Each encounter asks the player to observe a small behavior, choose a tool, and close the distance. The show framing makes these pursuits feel like episodes with their own set pieces. Between captures, exploration rewards curiosity through collectibles and hidden routes, giving completion-minded players reasons to look beyond the main chase.
A sequel that grows by changing context

GameSpot reported Sony’s announcement that Ape Escape 3 would arrive in North American stores on 17 January 2006. Its 30 November 2005 first-impressions article described the new transformations and monkey-catching action. The game’s strongest contribution is not an isolated mechanic but the way the broadcast conceit makes varied stages and abilities feel like parts of one playful production. Each new set offers another chance to change the rules of the chase.
